source.reviewMethod: Both official NFRDI PDFs were downloaded directly and text-extracted locally for this review. No raw PDF or species table was retained. SHA-256 checksums below identify the exact downloaded files.

publication.originalLicense: CC BY-NC 4.0, stated in the original PDF footer
publication.erratumPdfLicense: CC BY-NC 4.0, stated in the erratum PDF footer
publication.erratumLandingPageFooter: The HTML landing page shows a general CC BY 4.0 site footer unless otherwise stated; the erratum PDF itself states CC BY-NC 4.0 and the journal policy is also noncommercial. Treat CC BY-NC 4.0 as the controlling article term pending publisher clarification.
publication.reuseDisposition: Research-only. Keep concise attributed findings and source metadata; do not republish source paragraphs, figures, tables, the year-by-center matrix or other copied table content. The noncommercial license does not establish permission for any commercial Bangwit use.

study.waterbody: Ibulao River, Ifugao, Cordillera Administrative Region; the article says the river drains into Magat Dam and covers parts of Ifugao and Isabela.
study.collectionPeriod: 2015–2019; the abstract says January to December across those years.
study.samplingFrame: NSAP-style fish landings monitored at centers in Lamut, Kiangan and Lagawe. The paper describes fish nets, fish traps and electrofishing as historical collection gears. Its table and text do not provide a complete date-by-site event log or center coordinates.

sourceReportedSummary.interpretation: Keep the count and origin/status categories source-reported. Eighteen table rows are not eighteen independently verified species-level identifications: the table includes four BFARCAR internal sample-code labels and one genus-only Nomorhamphus sp.; the source's own family totals conflict. The taxon-origin categories were not independently re-evaluated.

erratumFindings.explicitCorrectionScope: The erratum says it corrects an error and adds supporting paragraphs and tables, but it does not explicitly identify the original error in a correction statement. It adds DNA methods/results and year-by-landing-center tables.
erratumFindings.correctedLandingCenterTable: The original annual richness table labels the third row Ifugao despite the text describing Lamut, Kiangan and Lagawe. The erratum table labels the three centers Kiangan, Lagawe and Lamut; this supports treating the original Ifugao row label as a table-label error, not a fourth center.
erratumFindings.unmonitoredCell: The original text says there was no Kiangan monitoring in 2019 because of reduced NSAP enumerator budget, and explicitly warns its blank/zero catch must not be interpreted as no fish or no catch.
erratumFindings.yearByCenterMatrix: The erratum supplies a presence-mark matrix for the reported fish labels across centers and years 2015–2019. It is historical source evidence only; no complete sampling-event denominator or individual catch record accompanies the matrix. The matrix was not copied into this review.

dnaLimits: The erratum describes COI amplification and D-loop work, outsourced sequencing, and sequence editing/clustering software, but the reviewed table shows percent identity values rather than explicit GenBank accession identifiers or links to the study sequences.

The Zenarchopterus philippinus entries have reported identity values of 92.11%–94.14%, materially lower than the other three values. The paper does not give enough table-level reference/alignment detail to independently interpret these values; preserve the source assignments but hold them for a specialist review.

The sequence table uses the broad local name Bunog for the two Rhinogobius giurinus samples, but it does not explicitly map sample codes Ibulao 08 or Ibulao 13 to the separate BFARCAR_Bunog02_154 label in Table 1. Do not merge those records by name alone.
nameAndDataQualityIssues: The original Table 1 spells a carp label Carracius carracius; the erratum's annual matrix spells it Carrasius carrasius. Neither is silently replaced here with an authority name.
The abstract says 11 fish families; the original body and erratum say 12. The erratum does not explicitly state which count is corrected.
The paper calls the table both finfishes and invertebrates, but the reviewed table rows are finfish labels; no invertebrate list was established in this review.
spatialAndTemporalLimits: The study names landing centers and includes a map, but the reviewed text/tables provide no center coordinates or reusable river geometry.
This is historical landed-catch monitoring from 2015–2019, not a present-day inventory or survey of every reach, tributary, or upstream/downstream habitat.

Catch and dominant-species descriptions reflect gear, effort, center coverage and NSAP staffing; the article itself attributes a high goby catch in Kiangan to electrofishing and warns that a 2019 Kiangan monitoring gap is not zero fish. Do not treat landings as abundance or use described gear as fishing advice.

disposition.historicalWaterbodyEvidence: A bounded, historical Ifugao river landings survey with three named landing centers and a companion 2023 erratum.
disposition.reason: The journal supplies a useful regional freshwater lead and an erratum with molecular results, but reported taxa, origin labels, family totals, carp spelling, sample-code mapping and some DNA identities require further review. Both PDFs are noncommercial-only and no app-use approval exists. No app projection was made.

nextAction: Cross-check the source labels and reported barcode candidates against current fish taxonomy authorities without automatic replacement. Keep sequence identity values and sample-code-to-Table-1 links held; seek an eligible independent survey or item-specific Bangwit reuse permission before public projection.
